name: Parallel triangles
summary: Two parallel triangles between two phase-free Z-spiders equal one triangle.
description:
Two phase-free Z-spiders connected by two wires, each carrying a triangle pointing towards the first spider, equal a single triangle. In the 2018 paper of Ng and Wang this rule is replaced by [(TR10')](../triangle-z-pi-triangle/).

**Conventions.** The triangle is the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ read from its tip to its base: a triangle pointing towards the inputs is $|0\rangle\langle 0|+|0\rangle\langle 1|+|1\rangle\langle 1|$, and a triangle pointing towards the outputs is its transpose. It can be written as a Clifford+T ZX-diagram. The papers read diagrams from top to bottom, so their triangles pointing up point towards the inputs here. Scalars that the papers write as diagrams (such as a connected pair of phase-free Z- and X-spiders, which is $\sqrt 2$) are given here as numbers.
unchecked_reason: the triangle is not a generator of PyZX or ZXLive
